3. Supabase data model — tables Sarthak must create

These tables must exist and have the exact column definitions below before any API endpoints can be built. Create these in Supabase first. The frontend document has already been issued to Gokul referencing these schemas — do not deviate from the column names or types without coordinating with Gokul.
One row per student per skill. Upserted on every assessment submission. This is the central data object of the entire platform.
CHECK (band_score >= 0 AND band_score <= 9), NULL until first scored
CHECK (level IN ('A','B','C')), derived and stored on every upsert
NULL for Listening and Reading. Writing: {task, coherence, lexical, grammar}. Speaking: {fluency, lexical, grammar, pronunciation}

The frontend polls GET /api/diagnostic/status/:studentId. The simplest implementation is a Supabase view that queries student_competency_matrix and returns one boolean per skill. Sarthak can implement this as a Postgres view or a computed query in the route handler — either is acceptable.
bool_or(skill = 'listening' AND band_score IS NOT NULL) AS listening_scored,
bool_or(skill = 'reading' AND band_score IS NOT NULL) AS reading_scored,
bool_or(skill = 'writing' AND band_score IS NOT NULL) AS writing_scored,
bool_or(skill = 'speaking' AND band_score IS NOT NULL) AS speaking_scored,
AND bool_or(skill = 'reading' AND band_score IS NOT NULL)
AND bool_or(skill = 'writing' AND band_score IS NOT NULL)
AND bool_or(skill = 'speaking' AND band_score IS NOT NULL))

Every time a band_score is written to student_competency_matrix, the level column must be computed and stored. Apply this logic in the Matrix Writer before the upsert — do not leave level calculation to the frontend.

No AI involved. Scoring is deterministic: count correct answers, look up the IELTS band conversion table, return the band. This is the simplest pipeline and should be working before any AI integration is attempted.
Validate request body: student_id present, skill is 'listening' or 'reading', answers object has expected keys
Query diagnostic_questions table for the active question set for this skill. Extract answer_key per question.
For each question, compare student answer to answer_key. Count correct answers (raw score out of 6 for Listening, out of 4 for Reading in diagnostic).
Apply IELTS band conversion lookup (see Section 5.1 below). Derive level using deriveLevel() function.
INSERT row: student_id, skill, mode='diagnostic', band_score, raw_answers (the answers object), sub_scores=null, feedback_json=null, transcript=null
UPSERT: student_id + skill as unique key. Set band_score, level, increment assessments_count, set last_updated=now().
Respond with { ok: true, band_score, level }
The diagnostic Listening section has 6 questions, not the full 40. Scale accordingly. This is a simplified diagnostic conversion — not the full IELTS table.
Note on diagnostic vs full assessment scoring

These simplified conversion tables are for the diagnostic only. When full Listening (40 questions) and Reading (40 questions) assessments are built in a future sprint, use the official IELTS conversion tables. Paul will provide the official tables at that point.

Writing is scored by Claude API. The accuracy of this pipeline depends almost entirely on the quality of the system prompt. The system prompt below is the exact prompt Sarthak must use. Do not change it without Paul's approval — prompt changes directly affect score accuracy.
Validate: student_id present, text.length > 0. If word count < 60, return 400 error (Gokul's frontend should prevent this, but defend server-side too).
Build the messages array with the system prompt from Section 5.3 and the student's text as the user message. Model: claude-sonnet-4-20250514. max_tokens: 1000. Require JSON-only response.
POST to https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages. Set server-side timeout to 30 seconds. Handle 429 (rate limit) and 5xx errors with a single retry after 3 seconds.

Extract the content[0].text field. Strip any markdown code fences if present (```json ... ```). JSON.parse the result. Validate that all 4 keys are present: task, coherence, lexical, grammar — each with band_score (number) and feedback (string).
Overall = average of the 4 criterion band scores, rounded to nearest 0.5. Use: Math.round(avg * 2) / 2

INSERT: student_id, skill='writing', mode='diagnostic', band_score (overall), sub_scores (4 criterion scores as JSON), feedback_json (4 criterion feedback strings as JSON), transcript=null, raw_answers=null
UPSERT: student_id + 'writing'. Set band_score (overall), level (derived), sub_scores (criterion scores), increment assessments_count, last_updated=now().
Respond with full shape from Section 4.4.
5.3 Claude system prompt — Writing scorer (exact text, do not modify)
You are an experienced IELTS examiner with 10 years of marking experience.
You will receive a student writing sample. Score it against the four official
Score each criterion on the 0-9 IELTS band scale in 0.5 increments.
1. Task Achievement (TA) — does the response address the task fully?
2. Coherence and Cohesion (CC) — is the response logically organised?
3. Lexical Resource (LR) — is the vocabulary range and accuracy appropriate?
4. Grammatical Range and Accuracy (GRA) — are structures varied and accurate?
Return ONLY a valid JSON object with no preamble, no markdown, no explanation.
- Band 7-8: Good user. Handles complex language well.
- Band 5-6: Modest to competent user. Manages overall meaning, some errors.
- Band 3-4: Limited user. Coping range. Basic language only.
- Band 1-2: Intermittent user. Little communication possible.
Do not give every student a 6. Score honestly. A weak response should score 3-4.

Speaking is the most complex pipeline. It runs two sequential AI calls: first Whisper for transcription, then Claude for scoring. Both must succeed for the pipeline to complete. Total latency budget is 25 seconds maximum.
Validate: student_id present, audio file present, file size < 10MB, file MIME type is audio/webm or audio/mp4. If invalid, return 400 immediately.

Upload the audio file to the 'speaking-recordings' bucket with path: {student_id}/{timestamp}.webm. Store the public URL for future reference. This happens before Whisper so we have a permanent copy regardless of transcription outcome.
POST to https://api.openai.com/v1/audio/transcriptions. Model: whisper-1. Language: 'en'. Response format: 'text'. Send the audio file as multipart/form-data. Set timeout: 20 seconds.
On success: store transcript string. On error or empty transcript: return { ok: false, error: 'Could not transcribe audio. Please try again.' } — do not proceed to Claude.
Build the messages array with the Speaking system prompt from Section 5.4, injecting the transcript as the user message. Model: claude-sonnet-4-20250514. max_tokens: 1000. Require JSON-only response.
POST to https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages. Timeout: 20 seconds. Single retry on 429 or 5xx.
Same parsing logic as Writing. Validate 4 keys: fluency, lexical, grammar, pronunciation — each with band_score and feedback.
Average of 4 criterion scores, rounded to nearest 0.5.
INSERT: student_id, skill='speaking', mode='diagnostic', band_score, sub_scores, feedback_json, transcript (the full Whisper transcript string), raw_answers=null
UPSERT: student_id + 'speaking'. Set band_score, level, sub_scores, increment assessments_count, last_updated=now().
Respond with full shape from Section 4.5 including transcript field.
{ ok: true, band_score, sub_scores, feedback, transcript }
5.4 Claude system prompt — Speaking scorer (exact text, do not modify)
You are an experienced IELTS Speaking examiner. You will receive a transcript of
a student's spoken response to an IELTS Part 1 prompt.
Score the response against the four official IELTS Speaking band descriptors.
Score each criterion on the 0-9 IELTS band scale in 0.5 increments.
1. Fluency and Coherence (FC) — flow of speech, logical organisation, absence of hesitation
2. Lexical Resource (LR) — vocabulary range, precision, natural use
3. Grammatical Range and Accuracy (GRA) — variety of structures, accuracy
4. Pronunciation (P) — clarity, intonation, stress patterns (infer from transcript where possible)
Note: Pronunciation must be estimated from the transcript. Look for evidence of
disfluency markers (um, uh, ...) and sentence-level clarity as proxies.
Return ONLY a valid JSON object with no preamble, no markdown, no explanation.
- Band 7+: Speaks at length with only rare repetition, uses flexible vocabulary naturally.
- Band 5-6: Mostly able to maintain flow, uses circumlocution, some repetition.
- Band 3-4: Responds but cannot sustain at length, restricted range, frequent errors.
Score honestly. A hesitant, limited response should score 3-4, not 5-6.
Every scoring pipeline ends with a call to the Matrix Writer. This is a shared utility function
writes once and calls from all four scoring routes. It must be idempotent — calling it twice with the same student_id and skill must not create duplicate rows.
async function writeToMatrix({ student_id, skill, band_score, sub_scores }) {
// Upsert: insert or update based on (student_id, skill) unique constraint
// Increment assessments_count using Postgres function, not client-side
// Increment assessments_count via RPC to avoid race conditions
if (error) throw new Error('Matrix write failed: ' + error.message);
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION increment_assessments_count(p_student_id uuid, p_skill text)
WHERE student_id = p_student_id AND skill = p_skill;

Claude JSON parsing failure — Claude will occasionally return JSON with a markdown code fence (```json ... ```) despite instructions not to. Sarthak must strip these defensively before JSON.parse. Never trust the raw response string.

Whisper empty transcript on silent audio — A student who records silence or background noise will get an empty transcript. Handle this case: if transcript.trim().length === 0, return 400 with message 'No speech detected. Please re-record.'
CORS — the Express server must allow requests from Gokul's frontend origin (localhost:3000 in dev, the production domain in prod). Set up CORS middleware before integration testing starts.
Supabase service role key vs anon key — all server-side Supabase calls must use the SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, not the anon key. The anon key is for client-side use only and will fail on protected tables.
OpenAI Whisper file format — Whisper v3 accepts webm and mp4. If Gokul's recorder produces a different format, the API call will fail. Confirm the frontend output format before integration testing.
Both the OpenAI Whisper call and the Claude API call incur per-call costs. For the diagnostic sprint, this is acceptable
, We need to use hugging face models parallelly to keep as fallbacks.
Do not add caching or deduplication logic in this sprint — that is a later optimisation.
